intro: Maximizing and evaluating noisy action values with the same estimator can introduce overestimation. Double Q targets separate which action is chosen from how it is valued.
task: Select actions using the online estimates, then look up those actions in the target estimates to construct a batch of bootstrap targets.
requirements: rewards and terminated have length B; online_next and target_next have identical shape (B,A). terminated is numeric zero/one and discount is in [0,1].

Choose actions=argmax(online_next,axis=1), breaking exact ties toward the lowest action index. Return {"actions": an integer NumPy vector, "targets": rewards+discount*(1-terminated)*target_next[rows,actions]}.
Select actions even for terminal rows, but suppress their bootstrap values. Do not maximize the target estimator independently or average the two estimators.

Use real finite numeric inputs of magnitude at most 1e30, excluding boolean parameters. Vectors have 1..256 entries and each matrix axis has length 1..256 unless a stricter bound is stated. Leave caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Keep the roles separate
hints.body: The online matrix selects the column; the target matrix supplies its value.

hints.title: Test disagreeing estimators
hints.body: Equal rankings cannot reveal the mistake of taking max(target_next).

explanation: If the estimators disagree about the best action, Double Q uses the target value at the online-selected action, even when that is not the target maximum.
This exercise computes the target from supplied estimates. Network updates, replay, and target-network synchronization belong to the surrounding training system.
